title: Brine management and disposal
bottleneck: Desalination produces about 1.5x more brine than freshwater — 142 million cubic meters daily — and this super-salty, chemical-laden waste is mostly dumped back into the sea, where it sinks and smothers marine life. Regulations are tightening, inland plants have nowhere to put it, and zero-liquid-discharge is technically possible but roughly doubles costs. Brine is desalination's waste crisis, growing with every new plant. Most brine is ocean-discharged with diffuser mitigation, but regulations are tightening and inland plants have nowhere to put it.
why_it_blocks: Scaling desalination without solving brine trades water scarcity for marine ecological collapse — an unacceptable bargain at planetary scale. Scaling desalination without solving brine trades water scarcity for marine ecological collapse.
current_state: Most brine is ocean-discharged with diffuser mitigation; brine valorization through mineral extraction is pilot-scale.
